subject: Science

source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 19 (Alveolus diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 19: Gas exchange in the alveoli. To understand how the alveoli are adapted for gas exchange by diffusion

picture.alt: A diagram of gas exchange at an alveolus
picture.draw: Draw and label: Alveolus diagram sheet

questions.q: Which way does carbon dioxide diffuse at the alveoli, and why?
questions.a: From the blood into the alveolus, because its concentration is higher in the blood.
questions.model: Find where it is high: carbon dioxide is high in the blood (made by respiration). Find where it is low: the air in the alveolus. Diffusion goes from high to low. So blood to alveolus.

questions.a: For example: large surface area; thin walls; good blood supply.

questions.q: Why do people with emphysema feel breathless?
questions.a: Damaged alveoli give less surface area, so less oxygen enters the blood.

questions.q: Core: Draw an alveolus with a capillary. Add arrows for oxygen and carbon dioxide and label three adaptations.
questions.a: Arrows: oxygen into blood, carbon dioxide out; labels: thin wall, large surface, capillary network.
questions.model: Teacher draws the first arrow: oxygen from the air sac into the capillary, labelled 'high to low'.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why a person needs millions of alveoli rather than one big sac.
questions.a: Many small sacs give a much larger surface area for the same volume, so diffusion is faster.

questions.q: Stretch: Use your breathing rate data: why does breathing rate rise during activity?
questions.a: Muscles respire faster, needing more oxygen and making more carbon dioxide, so gases must be exchanged faster.

questions.q: Oxygen diffuses from the alveoli into the...
Big question: how does oxygen get from the air into your blood?
questions.a: By diffusion across the thin, moist walls of the alveoli into the capillaries.
